docs.title: Mapping with Kids
docs.text:
Hands-on courses and activities in maps, satellites and code for children in Bengaluru, taught by Geospatial Specialist Sonia Das.

Children learn the way people who make maps for a living work. They use real data about places they know, make maps that answer questions, and finish with something they built themselves.

docs.title: From Paper to Map
docs.text:
A mapping activity for ages 10+

Become a neighbourhood mapper. Draw what you know about your streets on a paper map, then watch your drawing appear on a digital map of the world.

Taught by Sonia Das, Geospatial Specialist, Bengaluru.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Children know their neighbourhood better than any map does: the shortcut behind the shops, the park with the good swings, the corner that floods when it rains. In this two-hour activity they walk around the neighbourhood, mark what they find on a printed street map, and then see a computer turn their drawing into real map data.

docs.title: Who is this for
docs.text:
• Children aged 10+
  • No prior mapping or computer experience needed

docs.title: In two hours, your child will
docs.text:
1. Spot the parks, water, shops and shortcuts only locals know
  2. Draw them on a printed street map with a colour-coded key
  3. Photograph the map and see a computer turn it into real map data
  4. Compare their drawing with satellite images of the same streets

Tools they'll meet: a free website that reads hand-drawn maps, and real map-making software to see everyone's drawings on one map.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
When Every Saturday, from 24 October 2026 Time 10 am to 12 noon (2 hours) Ages 10+

Please note

This activity involves walking around the neighbourhood and collecting data. Comfortable shoes and a water bottle are a good idea.

docs.title: Mapping with Kids
docs.text:
A hands-on GIS course for kids. Learn how satellites see the Earth, then build a real map of India from scratch.

Taught by Sonia Das, Geospatial Specialist, Bengaluru.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GIS (Geographic Information Systems) is the technology behind every map app, weather map and delivery route. In this course children use a free, web-based GIS tool to make their own maps from real data. They start with an outline of India and a satellite view, and by the last session they turn their maps into interactive maps they can click and explore.

No experience is needed. Each session builds on the one before it.

docs.title: Who is this for
docs.text:
• Children aged 10+
  • No prior mapping or computer experience needed
  • Curious about places, satellites, or how maps are made

docs.title: What your child will build
docs.text: Session Project What they learn 1 Map of India Outline, style and a satellite view. How satellites photograph the Earth, and what a map layer is. 2 Famous Places Landmarks as dots, coloured and labelled. How every place on Earth has an address made of latitude and longitude. 3 Near or Far? Distance zones around their own city. How to ask a map a question and get an answer. 4 Interactive Maps Maps you can click, zoom and explore. How to turn their map into an interactive web map they can share.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A laptop with a web browser (Chrome or Edge)
  • An internet connection
  • No software to install

docs.title: Schedule and fee
docs.text: When 2 weekends, Saturday and Sunday, 1 hour each Starts 24 October 2026 Ages 10+ Fee Rs 2,000 per child, for all 4 sessions Also included Lifelong mentorship for a project of their choice. If your child gets curious about a topic and wants to explore it with maps, I will gladly guide them through it.
